Start Codex or Claude in one explicit existing empty shell pane with the owned hooks, after resolving the pane's seat. Launch never registers, accepts or ACKs: the handoff is read through the hooks

Usage: herdr-threads launch [OPTIONS] --kind <KIND> [-- <AGENT_ARG>...]

Arguments:
  [AGENT_ARG]...  Native agent arguments, kept byte for byte and in order after `--`

Options:
      --space <SPACE>
          Exact workspace ID or label; omitted inherits the caller's live workspace, never focus
      --state-dir <STATE_DIR>
          Select the local herdr-threads state directory. May repeat with an identical value; conflicting values are refused
      --host-endpoint <HOST_ENDPOINT>
          Select the local Herdr host socket path. May repeat with an identical value; conflicting values are refused
      --tab <TAB>
          Exact tab ID or label in the selected workspace; a tab ID supplies its workspace
      --json
          Emit a structured JSON result on stdout
      --pane <PANE>
          Exact pane ID, label or live agent name in the selected tab. Omitted parents inherit the live caller; outside Herdr supply parents or a pane ID. Qualify duplicate names with --space/--tab or use an ID; conflicts never pick a pane
      --human
          Human-readable tables and transcripts (the default on a terminal)
      --kind <KIND>
          Native agent to start [possible values: claude, codex, hermes, agy, synthetic_fourth]
      --harness-binary <PATH>
          Absolute harness executable whose `--version` is gated (default: the first `claude`/`codex` on PATH, which Herdr starts by name)
      --machine
          The stable `key: value` text form for scripts and models (the default when stdout is not a terminal)
      --cooperative-seat <COOPERATIVE_SEAT>
          Explicit seat ID for a cooperative agent call; requires all four --cooperative-* options
      --name <NAME>
          Herdr agent name (default: the pane's Herdr label, else the compact seat ID, or `seat-<short seat id>` for a persisted seat). Fitted to Herdr's `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`
      --cooperative-target <COOPERATIVE_TARGET>
          Exact live pane ID or scoped name bound to the cooperative seat
      --cooperative-harness <COOPERATIVE_HARNESS>
          Agent harness making the cooperative call [possible values: claude, codex, hermes, agy, synthetic_fourth]
      --cooperative-role <COOPERATIVE_ROLE>
          Agent role for the cooperative call [possible values: top-level, subagent]
      --agent-id <ID>
          Subagent agent id, inserted by herdr-threads' Claude PreToolUse hook (spec §1). Carried into the cooperative claim; no behaviour change until session bindings land
  -h, --help
          Print help

Target:
  --pane names one existing Herdr pane at its interactive shell prompt; launch never
  creates, splits or picks a pane and never types into an occupied one. Herdr's
  guarded `agent start` refuses a busy pane.

Preflight (nothing is started when any step refuses):
  - the selected executable must resolve; its registered contract is declared without
    invoking --version, --help or schema probes, and runtime metadata remains unknown;
  - the pane's seat is resolved like `seat resolve --pane`; a recovery-held target
    needs `seat rebind ... --operator` or a fresh seat first;
  - the owned user-level hooks must be set up (`herdr-threads setup HARNESS`) in the
    settings or hook file of the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CODEX_HOME / HOME the agent
    will use (an absolute one the pane's shell exports, else launch's own, else HOME;
    the report's config_dir names it);
  - a last fresh read of the pane just before Herdr starts the agent.

Agent name: --name NAME, else the pane's Herdr label, else s<short seat id>
for a new compact ID (seat-<short seat id> for a persisted ID),
fitted to Herdr's [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}. If another live agent holds it, launch
retries once with -<short seat id> appended.

Arguments after `--` are passed to the agent unchanged and in order. Optional
HERDR_THREADS_CLAUDE_OPTS / HERDR_THREADS_CODEX_OPTS / HERDR_THREADS_AGY_OPTS are prepended to those arguments;
unset or empty adds nothing. Use shell-style quotes and escapes; variables and
commands are never expanded.
The combined arguments use the same managed-launch guards. The owned configuration
is on disk, so launch adds no hook or daemon-mode arguments by default.
Native options that would replace the owned configuration are refused. No
auto-approve flag is added.

Launch is not receipt: it never checks in, accepts or ACKs. Invitations and messages
sent before launch stay pending; the agent's SessionStart hook shows them, and
`herdr-threads inbox --seat SEAT` lists them even when the initial prompt is lost.
After an observed start, the seat gets a `managed_launch` placeholder binding next to
any it already holds (report `binding`; `seat inspect` shows it as launched, not checked
in): it lets the daemon wake the idle agent for pending work before its first check-in
(some harnesses run no SessionStart hook until their first turn), and the launched
harness's first check-in replaces it. It is not recorded when Herdr shows no single
started process.

A harness that exits right after the start (for example a harness refusing its arguments)
fails launch at once with invalid_request and the pane's last lines.

Harness choices come from the same-binary registry.

Codex launches report
`codex`: the effective CODEX_HOME, its config.toml and the selected profile (-p/--profile,
else `profile` in config.toml, else default). Codex CLI commands use approved
outside-sandbox execution, without a network/socket allowance. Unsupported Codex subcommands,
an explicit `--daemon`, a caller `--no-daemon` after the subcommand and a caller `-c hooks.*`
override are refused.

Hermes is experimental, natively
measured on 0.21.5 with a private Herdr build; a bare Hermes CLI session also
joins through its hooks; this launch adds the guarded process hint that lets Herdr
recognize it. Its separate startup/profile/API prelaunch observation
must match the selected executable, owned generation and configured enabled profile.
Native Hermes -p/--profile NAME after `--` is emitted once (default when omitted);
--cli and one policy-owned chat token compose the captured interactive grammar.
Known-arity model/provider options and chat -q/--query are supported in their native
positions. Resume, TUI/native/oneshot, arbitrary subcommands, plugin suppression and
approval bypass forms refuse. Launch never enables a plugin or grants native consent.
The private host must support guarded process hints; a hint or observed launch is
neither callback activation nor model consumption. Hermes hooks run in its gateway, so
no idle wake reaches the seat yet; no composer stash/restore.

agy launch accepts --add-dir, --agent, --conversation, --effort, --mode, --model, --project, --log-file, -i/--prompt-interactive, -c/--continue and --new-project (Go flag grammar: --name value or --name=value). It refuses -p/--print/--prompt, --dangerously-skip-permissions, --sandbox, --remote-control, the print-only flags, single-dash long forms, unknown flags, positionals, subcommands, `--`, and -c together with --conversation. -c continues the most recent conversation; it is not an alias of --conversation. Extra arguments come from HERDR_THREADS_AGY_OPTS in the same grammar.

Exit status: 0 startup observed; 5 start may have happened but was not confirmed:
inspect the pane (`herdr agent get` / `herdr agent read`) before launching again.
